fields.mechanism: Integrated radial hybrid magnetic bearing providing contactless suspension via magnetic force fields to eliminate mechanical friction and thermal coupling.
fields.intervention: Replace the reaction wheel's mechanical contact bearings with an integrated radial hybrid magnetic bearing system, utilizing active magnetic field control to decouple the rotor from the housing and prevent stall due to low-temperature lubricant viscosity changes.
fields.expected_effect: The bearing stall at low temperatures is eliminated because magnetic suspension does not rely on liquid lubricants or mechanical contact, removing the thermal dependence of friction on the shadowing event.
fields.falsification_test: Perform a single on-orbit test by commanding the reaction wheel to a sustained high-speed rotation specifically during the low-temperature phase of the orbital shadow; if the wheel maintains constant angular velocity without intermittent stalls, the mechanical bearing stall hypothesis is falsified.
fields.mechanism_source_span: Novel Integrated Radial Hybrid Magnetic Bearing

candidate.falsification_test: Perform a single on-orbit test by commanding the reaction wheel to a sustained high-speed rotation specifically during the low-temperature phase of the orbital shadow; if the wheel maintains constant angular velocity without intermittent stalls, the mechanical bearing stall hypothesis is falsified.

fields.mechanism: Integrated radial hybrid magnetic bearing providing contactless rotor support
fields.intervention: Command the reaction wheel motor to operate in a magnetic suspension mode using the integrated radial hybrid magnetic bearing, eliminating mechanical bearing contact during eclipse thermal transients.
fields.expected_effect: Elimination of low-temperature bearing stall and associated attitude drift by removing physical contact surfaces subject to lubricant viscosity increase or differential thermal contraction.
fields.falsification_test: Command the reaction wheel to spin up from rest exclusively on magnetic bearing support during orbital eclipse; if intermittent stall persists without mechanical contact, the thermal-stall coupling is not solely mechanical bearing friction.
